tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session navigates to Magento admin product grid, logs in (performed outside this tool), analyzes the grid controls, fills multiple filters (name, sku, id-range, price-range, qty-range, selects), clicks Search, selects rows for mass-action, opens product edit page and exercises Add Product. We reproduced the filter and edit flows and recorded stable selectors and elementHash fallbacks.

Task Definition:
- This tool's single purpose: apply given product-finding criteria on the Magento Admin product grid and open the first matching product's Edit page, returning both the filtered result set and the edit-page field selector summary for automation.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to product grid URL.
2) Wait for grid to load.
3) Populate each filter control with the corresponding input parameter (empty string leaves the control blank). We use recorded elementHash values (where available) as deterministic fallbacks and attribute-based selectors (name, id, th-scoped XPaths) as primary selectors.
4) Click the Search button and wait for the grid to refresh.
5) Extract filtered rows and Edit link hrefs.
6) Click the Edit link of the first filtered row and wait for the Edit page.
7) Extract the Edit page fields and recommended stable selectors.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- base_url (required): product grid URL; used as first navigation target.
- name, sku, id_from, id_to, price_from, price_to, qty_from, qty_to: textual values for corresponding grid filters.
- sType, attribute_set, visibility, status, website, currency: dropdown/select visible text values to pick in filters.
- open_first_match (bool): whether to open the first match after extraction (tool always attempts to click first Edit link; set true to do so, false can be used by consumers to ignore subsequent click result if needed).

Step Optimization:
- Deterministic selectors: when available use attribute-based selectors (input[name='sku'], input[name='name'], select[name='type'], select[name='set']) — these are stable across Magento 1.x admin instances. Recorded elementHash values are included to guarantee deterministic targeting in environments where the exact element positions recorded match the runtime DOM.
- Navigation optimization: we keep direct navigation to the product grid; we do not attempt to build complex query-string URLs because Magento admin grids typically apply filters via POST/AJAX and the recorded UI interaction is more reliable across admin customizations.
- Removed non-essential exploratory steps: we only perform the necessary steps to apply filters and open the first match. We do not re-run broad page analyses or extra pagination/sorting actions.

Edge cases and notes:
- If the admin uses native window.confirm for mass-actions, it cannot be controlled via DOM selectors; the test driver must accept the dialog. This tool does not execute destructive mass-actions.
- The tool assumes the user is already authenticated in the browser session or that the provided base_url is accessible without re-authentication (per instructions). Do not include login steps here.
- Wait steps are conservative (1-2 seconds). Callers should implement explicit waits for grid tbody rows or success messages in real automation runners (Playwright/Selenium) to avoid flakiness.

Conclusion:
- The tool provides a compact, repeatable sequence to find products by flexible criteria and open the first matching product for editing. It prefers attribute-based selectors and includes recorded elementHash fallbacks for robustness.
name: magento_find_and_open_product
description: Navigate to Magento admin product grid, apply product-finding filters (id range, name, sku, type, attribute set, price/qty ranges, visibility, status, website), click Search, extract the first matching row and open its Edit page. Returns product-grid results and product edit page summary/selectors. Uses stable attribute-based selectors and recorded elementHashes as deterministic fallbacks.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento admin product grid (Manage Products).
Wait for the page and grid to load.
Fill the Name filter input. Uses the recorded elementHash as deterministic fallback; CSS targets the filter input by name.
Fill the SKU filter input (partial or full).
Fill the ID 'From' filter input (use name='id[from]').
steps.cssSelector: table.grid thead tr:nth-of-type(2) th:nth-of-type(2) input[name='id[from]'], input[name='id[from]']

steps.description: Fill the ID 'To' filter input (use name='id[to]').
steps.cssSelector: table.grid thead tr:nth-of-type(2) th:nth-of-type(2) input[name='id[to]'], input[name='id[to]']

steps.description: Set the Type filter by visible text (e.g. 'Simple Product'). Uses recorded elementHash as fallback.
Set the Attribute Set filter by visible text (e.g. 'Default').
Fill the Price 'From' filter input.
Fill the Price 'To' filter input.
Select the Price currency (if present).
Fill the Qty 'From' filter input.
Fill the Qty 'To' filter input.
Set the Visibility filter by visible text (e.g. 'Catalog, Search').
Set the Status filter by visible text (e.g. 'Enabled' or 'Disabled').
Set the Website filter by visible text (e.g. 'Main Website').
Click the Search button to apply filters. Uses recorded elementHash as deterministic fallback.
Wait for grid to refresh and for rows to load after applying filters.
Capture resulting product rows and Edit link hrefs to pick a product to open for editing.
steps.goal: Extract filtered rows: product id, name, sku, price, qty, visibility, status and edit link for each visible row (first 20).

steps.description: Click the Edit link of the first matching result (first visible row). This uses an XPath that looks for edit href pattern; the CSS selector is a fallback.
Wait for the product Edit page to load.
Return the edit page fields and recommended selectors for automation.
steps.goal: Extract product edit page summary and stable selectors for Name, SKU, Price, Qty, Status, Visibility, Websites and Save/Back buttons.

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base URL for the Magento admin product grid (example: "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/")

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Product name filter (partial or full). Enter empty string to leave blank.

input_schema.name: sku
input_schema.description: Product SKU filter (partial or full). Enter empty string to leave blank.

input_schema.name: id_from
input_schema.description: Product ID 'From' numeric filter. Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: id_to
input_schema.description: Product ID 'To' numeric filter. Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: price_from
input_schema.description: Price filter lower bound (e.g. '10'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: price_to
input_schema.description: Price filter upper bound (e.g. '100'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: qty_from
input_schema.description: Quantity filter lower bound. Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: qty_to
input_schema.description: Quantity filter upper bound. Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: sType
input_schema.description: Product Type filter visible text (e.g. 'Simple Product'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: attribute_set
input_schema.description: Attribute Set filter visible text (e.g. 'Default'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: Visibility filter visible text (e.g. 'Catalog, Search'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Status filter visible text (e.g. 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: website
input_schema.description: Website filter visible text (e.g. 'Main Website'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: currency
input_schema.description: Currency visible text for Price filter (example: 'USD'). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: open_first_match
input_schema.description: If true, open the first grid row's Edit link after applying filters. If false, only return extracted filtered rows.
